'''Matcha Flavoured 1.12.6-alpha''', "Poplar Drop", is the current version of [[Matcha Flavoured]], published on October 14, 2026, four days after [[Matcha Flavoured 1.12.5|1.12.5]]. It is an alpha for ''Minecraft'' 26.3: its <code>pack.mcmeta</code> reports the version as "1.12.6 for 26.3", while 1.12.5 was a full release for 26.2.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/pack.mcmeta}}</ref> It is the first release of the pack's 26.3 port since the [[Matcha Flavoured 1.12.3|1.12.3]] alpha for 26.3, so besides the changes in its release notes it brings everything the port added after the 26.2 releases: [[poplar]] trees, [[cushion]]s, [[abandoned camp]]s, reworked swamps and more. The newest full release is still 1.12.5, for 26.2.

The release notes say that an earlier upload was taken off Modrinth after a reported game-breaking bug, which turned out not to be real, and that the developer fixed other bugs while it was down.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=I deleted the old version off of modrinth, I had a major bug reported--game breaking--I feaked out, deleted it, and scrambled to fix it. Turns out actually it wasn't real. My bad}}</ref>

== Major additions and changes ==
=== Husks and Hunger ===
* [[Husk]]s deal 6 damage ({{Hp|6}}) instead of 10 on Normal.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/normal_modifications/modify_husk.mcfunction}}</ref>
* The Hunger effect, which husks inflict, now does something: on Normal and Hard, a player with Hunger can't regenerate, so [[food]] doesn't heal until it wears off. An action-bar meter counts down its remaining time. Easy is exempt.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/regeneration/mark_player.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/hunger/effect.mcfunction}}</ref> To make room for this, the pack no longer gives players a hidden Hunger effect to hold their food bar down; it only tops the bar up with Saturation when it falls to 8 or lower.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/manage_hunger.mcfunction}}</ref> See [[Hunger]].
* Foods with the "Cleanse Maleffect" [[intrinsic]], such as [[bread]], [[Honey Ginger Tea|honey ginger tea]] and [[Ice Cream|ice cream]], also remove Hunger.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/mob_effect/harmful.json}}</ref>

=== Wither ===
{{Main|Wither effect}}
* The [[Wither effect]] takes a heart after 9 seconds on Normal and 6 seconds on Hard, instead of 8 seconds on both.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/wither/effect_normal.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/wither/effect_hard.mcfunction}}</ref>
* [[Shakudo equipment|Shakudo armor]] gives wither resistance, which adds time to that timer: each piece counts, up to four, and the [[Elytra#Shakudo Elytra|shakudo elytra]] gives the full amount by itself. On Normal, one piece outlasts a single [[Wither Skeleton|wither skeleton]] hit.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/enchantment_effects/shakudo_effects/wither_resistance/apply_resistance.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=One piece of shakudo is now enough to prevent heatbreaker from a wither skeleton hit (in normal), but if you are hit more than once while withered, it will not save you}}</ref>
* Shakudo armor's [[Cleanse|cleanse]] no longer removes Wither.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/enchantment_effects/shakudo_effects/cleanse/maleffect.mcfunction}}</ref>
* [[Milk Bottle|Milk bottles]] are drunk twice as fast (0.8 seconds instead of 1.6), which the notes suggest as preparation against the Wither.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/crafting/milk_bottle.json}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=Milk Bottles are now fast to drink, good trade off for anti-wither prep}}</ref>

=== Renamed items ===
* Divine Fragment (the turtle scute) is renamed [[Pith]], and Divine Favor (the nether star) [[Amalgamated Pith]]. The release notes don't mention it.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref> See [[Renamed items]].

=== From the 26.3 port ===
These come from the pack's 26.3 branch and are new compared with 1.12.5. Most were first published in the 1.12.3 alpha for 26.3:
* [[Poplar]] trees and their wood, in red, orange and yellow, with stonecutter recipes, a sapling recipe from leaves and a [[Lumberjack|lumberjack]] trade. See [[Biomes]].
* Swamps with their own trees, bushes and shelf [[Mushroom|mushrooms]], and the dappled forest's closed canopy.
* [[Abandoned camp]]s, whose chests and barrels have the pack's own loot, with camp maps and buried structure maps. The Archaeologist's [[Explorer maps|explorer maps]] are built on ''Minecraft'' 26.3's separate map items, and most show their structure's marker.
* [[Cushion]]s, and [[stonecutter]] recipes that cut wool and concrete into slabs and stairs, and wool into carpets and cushions.
* [[Clear Mushroom Soup|Clear mushroom soup]], from milking a mooshroom with a bowl, and the 26.3 [[Rabbit Stew|rabbit stew]] recipe with a shelf mushroom.
* The reworked [[Amnestic]], used on a villager instead of placed.
* Reworked [[Trailblaze]], [[Zephyr]], [[Divinity]] and [[Set bonus|shakudo regeneration]] effects.
* Empty village loot tables (see [[Chest loot#Village]]), changed [[Carrot|carrot]] and [[Hematite|deepslate hematite]] drops, and unfinished groundwork for [[Bobwhite|bobwhites]].

=== Textures ===
* New textures for the shipwreck, trail ruins, [[Papal Outpost|papal outpost]] and [[Abbey]] maps.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=Textures for Shipwreck, Trail ruin, papal outpost, and Abbey maps all updated}}</ref>
* [[Leaves|Leaf]] textures changed "for optimisation reasons".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=Leaf textures changed for optimisation reasons}}</ref>
* A jungle shelf texture, which was missing, and fixes to some emoji glyphs.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/textures/block/jungle_shelf.png}}</ref>

=== Other changes ===
* [[Ice Cream|Ice cream]] no longer leaves a bowl.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/food/matcha/ice_cream.json}}</ref>
* Food recipes on [[kindling]] take 200 ticks instead of 100, as do the [[Mud Kiln|mud kiln]]'s and the [[Blast Furnace|blast furnace]]'s recipes. Vanilla 26.3 doubles its own smoker and blast furnace recipe times the same way.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/campfire/cooked_beef.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/kiln/charred_meat.json}}</ref>
* The pack no longer revokes advancements when a world is updated; the notes say this was only needed for 1.12.3 and 1.12.4.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=Removed Advancment revokations on update, this was only needed for 1.12.3+4 so it has been removed}}</ref> Advancements that the pack uses as triggers are instead revoked when the pack loads and when a player joins.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/player_joined.mcfunction}}</ref>
* Some [[favorite food]] trades ask for 4 or 8 of the food instead of 1, such as 8 brachio chicken nuggets for an emerald.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/favorite_food/food_trades/food_2.mcfunction}}</ref>

== Fixes ==
The release notes list these fixes. Most were bugs of the 1.12.3 alpha for 26.3 that the 26.2 releases had already fixed or never had:
* Straw beds work. They are a ''Minecraft'' 26.3 block, and the pack's texture for them was added.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/textures/block/straw_bed.png}}</ref>
* Treasure maps from shipwrecks and ocean ruins lead to buried treasure; in the 26.3 alpha they led to woodland mansions. See [[Explorer maps]].
* [[Chocolate]] stacks, as it has on 26.2 since [[Matcha Flavoured 1.12.4|1.12.4]].
* Curries and [[Tonkotsu Ramen|tonkotsu ramen]] can't be cooked on kindling, as on 26.2 since 1.12.5.

== Known issues ==
The release notes warn that some foods may be inedible: old foods "maybe", vanilla foods (from the creative menu) unless they update themselves, raw meats, and sometimes modded foods, which a datapack can't fix. They ask players who find a newly made food that can't be eaten to report it.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=Raw meats will be inedible}}</ref> The pack's own foods have no food component and can always be eaten, but vanilla foods keep theirs, and since the pack no longer holds the food bar down, they can't be eaten while it is full. See [[Known bugs]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/manage_hunger.mcfunction}}</ref>

== Credits ==
The repository's changelog keeps the credits of 1.12.5, with more thanks to HapppySpud ("and much more"), Linkershim ("MANY other coding things") and Fpekal ("a TON on the 26.3 port"). See [[Credits]].<ref>{{Source|changelog.md}}</ref>
